title: Some / any / no — the traps
note: Builds on a1_some_any (basic + / − / ? rule). The Czech traps: žádný = no OR not…any, one negation only; free-choice any (jakýkoli); some-/any-/no- compounds. Split out of a1_some_any 2026-08-16 (was 52 items — trap material contaminated beginners' shuffled passes). Evidence: Tomas 'we have still any problems', Martina 'I bought any food', 'didn't have no drink'.

cards.title: You know the basic rule

table.caption: from Some / any (A1)
rows: I don't have any coffee. · Do you have any coffee?

points: This unit is about the three places Czech pulls you off that rule.

cards.title: no = not…any
points: English says the negative ONCE — Czech says it twice (nemám žádný).
no + noun → the verb stays positive.
Never two negatives: ~~I don't have no coffee~~.

cards.title: any in + = it doesn't matter which

table.caption: two different meanings
rows: real food I actually bought — NOT any

points: any in a positive sentence = jakýkoli / kdykoli / kamkoli.
A real specific thing = some: I bought some food, never ~~I bought any food~~.

cards.title: something · anything · nothing

table.caption: the same rule, one level up

points: I want something · I don't want anything · I want nothing.
Nobody / nothing / nowhere already contain the `no` — the verb stays positive.

cards.title: Common mistakes

table.caption: check
rows: I don't have any coffee. = I have no coffee.
I didn't say anything. = I said nothing.

points: žádný → no (positive verb) or not…any — never both negatives.
Real things you have, want or bought → some.
